```{r setup, include=TRUE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(readxl)
library(AER)  

df <- read_excel("C:\\Desktop\\AK1991.xlsx")

set.seed(42)
n        <- 250      # sample size per replication
B0       <- 1.0      # true coefficient
sigma_xi  <- 1.0     # std dev of measurement error in D1
sigma_eta <- 1.0     # std dev of measurement error in D2
n_sims   <- 10000    # number of Monte Carlo replications

# Storage vectors
coef_a <- numeric(n_sims)   # (a) OLS on true D
coef_b <- numeric(n_sims)   # (b) OLS on D1 (mismeasured)
coef_c <- numeric(n_sims)   # (c) IV: D1 instrumented by D2


# Monte Carlo Loop
for (i in 1:n_sims) {
  idx  <- sample(nrow(df), n, replace = TRUE)
  D    <- df$edu[idx]
#Structural error and outcomes
  eps  <- rnorm(n, 0, 1)
#True Model
  Y    <- D * B0 + eps
#Mismeasured versions of model
  xi   <- rnorm(n, 0, sigma_xi)
  eta  <- rnorm(n, 0, sigma_eta)
  D1   <- D + xi
  D2   <- D + eta

#a) OLS: Y on true D
coef_a[i] <- coef(lm(Y ~ D))[["D"]]

#b) OLS: Y on D1 (attenuation bias expected)
coef_b[i] <- coef(lm(Y ~ D1))[["D1"]]

#c) IV: instrument D1 with D2 (2SLS via ivreg)
coef_c[i] <- coef(ivreg(Y ~ D1 | D2))[["D1"]]
}


#Results
cat(sprintf("Parameters: B0 = %.1f | n = %d | n_sims = %d\n",
            B0, n, n_sims))
cat(sprintf("sigma_xi = %.1f | sigma_eta = %.1f\n\n",
            sigma_xi, sigma_eta))

cat(sprintf("(a) OLS on true D  – Median: %.4f\n", median(coef_a)))
cat(sprintf("(b) OLS on D1      – Median: %.4f\n", median(coef_b)))

# Theoretical attenuation factor
var_D       <- var(df$edu)
attenuation <- B0 * var_D / (var_D + sigma_xi^2)
cat(sprintf("    Theoretical: B0 * Var(D)/(Var(D)+sigma_xi^2) = %.4f\n",
            attenuation))

cat(sprintf("(c) IV  (D1 ~ D2)  – Median: %.4f\n\n", median(coef_c)))


# Plot: Density of the three estimators
xlim_range <- range(c(coef_a, coef_b, coef_c), na.rm = TRUE)
xlim_range <- c(max(xlim_range[1], -1), min(xlim_range[2], 3))

da <- density(coef_a)
db <- density(coef_b)
dc <- density(coef_c)

plot(da, col = "forestgreen", lwd = 2,
     xlim = xlim_range,
     ylim = c(0, max(da$y, db$y, dc$y) * 1.15),
     main = "Measurement Error Simulation (10,000 reps)",
     xlab = expression(hat(beta)[0]),
     ylab = "Density")
lines(db, col = "firebrick",  lwd = 2)
lines(dc, col = "steelblue",  lwd = 2)
abline(v = B0, lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)
abline(v = attenuation, lty = 3, col = "firebrick", lwd = 1.5)
legend("topright",
       legend = c(
         sprintf("(a) OLS true D  (med = %.3f)", median(coef_a)),
         sprintf("(b) OLS D1      (med = %.3f)", median(coef_b)),
         sprintf("(c) IV D1~D2    (med = %.3f)", median(coef_c)),
         sprintf("True B0 = %.1f", B0),
         sprintf("Theoretical att. = %.4f", attenuation)
       ),
       col    = c("forestgreen", "firebrick", "steelblue", "black", "firebrick"),
       lty    = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 3),
       lwd    = c(2, 2, 2, 1.5, 1.5),
       cex    = 0.8)


cat("Short Note\n")
cat(
"(a) OLS on the true regressor D is unbiased and consistent,
    recovering B0 = 1 precisely (median ~ 1.000).

(b) Replacing D with the mismeasured proxy D1 = D + xi introduces
    classical measurement error. OLS is no longer consistent: the
    estimate is attenuated (biased toward zero). The attenuation
    factor is Var(D) / (Var(D) + sigma_xi^2). With Var(edu) ~ 10.77
    and sigma_xi^2 = 1, theory predicts a factor of ~ 0.915, and
    the simulation median of ~ 0.915 confirms this exactly.

(c) Using the second noisy measure D2 = D + eta as an instrument for
    D1 corrects the attenuation bias. D2 is correlated with D1
    through the shared true D (relevance) but uncorrelated with xi
    (exclusion restriction), making it a valid instrument. The IV
    median ~ 1.000 recovers the true B0, consistent with theory.\n"
)

```
